what_this_is: The view files that the article's exon-map figure draws from. The exon rows are copied from ChannelScope evidence-graph records, and the highlights' coding values from the codon map table; the variant's position and change are ClinVar's, as retrieved. Three sequences are carried, each in its own FASTA file: the GRCh38 bases of the transcript's span, as read from NCBI; the exonic sequence; and P21817-1, as read from UniProt. The assembly's record is NCBI's, and the sources' terms are quoted from their pages. From v0.4: plain-language notes and highlight groups, every sentence with its source; HGVS's amino-acid table, and the rules a figure follows to name and class a typed change, quoted from HGVS Nomenclature 21.1.4 and the Sequence Ontology; ClinVar's classifications, quoted as ClinVar's; and two test sets, of HGVS c. names at chosen positions, in a file of its own, and of the consequences of chosen changes, which this release withholds (its README says why). New in v0.5: the typed-variant engine names an in-frame change that brings a stop after its first changed residue as HGVS does, and classes it stop_gained; its rules quote HGVS's protein forms that v0.4 computed without quoting, and settle the changes through the stop codon and the changes it refuses; and the test set holds 91 curated cases and 4 refused ones, with the engine's naming also checked on HGVS's own examples on their own transcripts. Worked out by the builder of exon_map_v0.5, whose data this release keeps, rather than copied: the counts under figures, from the 106 exon rows; the intronic highlights' positions, from the exon bounds by HGVS's +1 and -1 rule, with their bases read from the GRCh38 snapshot; the variant's alternate codon, which is the reference codon as read with ClinVar's alternate base put in, translated by the standard genetic code; the exonic sequence, which is the span's bases joined at the exon bounds, compared base for base with NCBI's and Ensembl's records of the transcript; the intronic c. names at the test positions; and every row of the typed-variant test set, compared with ClinVar's 379 expert-panel records, and with the answers of an independent implementation, whose results this release withholds. This reissue's checks, each with the faults planted to test it, and v0.5's 29 checks are listed in manifest.json. Check each file's sha256 against manifest.json before drawing.

assembly_scope: Only chromosome 19 of the Primary Assembly unit is used, as NC_000019.10. No patch scaffold and no alternate locus is used, and none lies in the transcript's span (check B12). Chromosome 19 is the same sequence in GRCh38 as first released as in GRCh38.p14 (check B11), so every coordinate here holds in both.

variant.note: The exon-map figure's worked example, as ClinVar records it in the summary retrieved below. It says where the variant sits and what it changes; it carries no classification. p_change is ClinVar's own, and like any p. description made from a c. change it is the predicted consequence. alt_codon is the reference codon as read, with the SPDI's alternate base put in; alt_aa is its translation, which check B5 requires to match ClinVar's. ClinVar's classification of it is quoted, as ClinVar's, in highlight_groups, group c1840.

figures.span_basis: first exon start to last exon end on GRCh38; exonic bases are the exons' own lengths, coding and untranslated alike

sequences.note: Three sequences, each in its own FASTA file: one header line beginning '>', then the whole sequence on a single line in upper case, then a newline. Every base and residue is read from a sequence record, none inferred (rule 8's state r). Positions follow by arithmetic, by each entry's position_rule. After parsing, a sequence's md5 and sequence_digest (refget) can be checked against the values here.

exonic.what: The transcript's 106 exons joined in order, untranslated ends included: the genomic span's bases at the exon table's bounds

exonic.position_rule: Exon n occupies transcript positions S + 1 to S + L, where L is its length (genome_end - genome_start + 1 in the exon table) and S is the sum of the lengths of the exons before it. A coding base c.N is transcript position N + 139.

sentences.text: HGNC, the HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee, approves unique symbols and names for human genes, so that each can be named without ambiguity.
Each gene it names has a stable HGNC ID, which stays the same even if the gene's symbol or name is updated.
RYR1's HGNC ID is HGNC:10483.
The Genome Reference Consortium (GRC) works to improve the human reference genome assembly, correcting errors and adding sequence.
In May 2022 it released GRCh38.p14, an update to the human reference assembly that does not change its coordinates.
An assembly is a set of chromosomes and other sequences used to represent an organism's genome, and most current assemblies are haploid, representing one set of chromosomes.
This figure's positions are on chromosome 19 of GRCh38, whose sequence is the same in GRCh38.p14, so every position holds in both.
RYR1 lies on the plus strand: its transcript reads chromosome 19's bases in the order the assembly writes them, so positions rise from exon 1 to exon 106.

A MANE Select transcript is a pair of identically annotated records, one from NCBI's RefSeq, with an NM_ identifier, and one from Ensembl, with an ENST identifier, which have identical sequence and splice structure and the same start and end coordinates.
The MANE Select set holds one transcript at each locus, representative of the biology there, and MANE calls it useful as a universal standard for clinical reporting.
RYR1's MANE Select pair is NM_000540.3 and ENST00000359596.8, and this release finds the two records identical at every one of the transcript's 15,400 bases.
HGVS, whose rules the figure's c. names follow, prefers the MANE Select transcript where it is a suitable reference for the variant described.
A UniProt isoform's identifier is its entry's accession, a dash and a number, so P21817-1 names an isoform of entry P21817.

For each entry UniProt displays one canonical sequence, chosen to meet at least one of five criteria, among them that it is functional, that it is widely expressed, or that it is identical to the sequence chosen by projects such as MANE.
For P21817 the sequence displayed is isoform 1, P21817-1.
sentences.location: The entry's alternative products: isoform 1, sequence status Displayed

sentences.text: P21817-1 and RefSeq's NP_000531.2 are the same sequence, so a residue number means the same residue in either.
Residue 1 is the methionine of the start codon, c.1 to c.3, which reads ATG.
An exon is a part of a gene's transcript that is not removed by RNA splicing.
Some exons are coding, carrying information for making a protein, and others are non-coding.
sentences.location: Talking Glossary, Exon: its definition, not the narration on the same page

sentences.text: The untranslated regions are the parts of a messenger RNA that lie before or after the sequence that is translated into protein.
RYR1's transcript NM_000540.3 is 15,400 bases long, the lengths of its 106 exons added together, and its coding sequence runs from position 140 to position 15,256.
So exon 1 holds 139 untranslated bases and then 45 coding ones, and exon 106 holds 96 coding bases and then 144 untranslated ones.

notes_basis: Plain-language notes on the four identifiers the exon-map figure names, and a fifth, 'not every exonic base codes', in the shape agreed for the article on 2026-10-03. Every sentence names its source: a page, by the URL that logged it, with link giving the page a reader opens where the URL is an API or a raw file; or the release, by file. The words a sentence rests on were found in that page as retrieved (check B18); they stay in ChannelScope's reading record. The date a page was read is its retrieval's, under provenance.

highlight_groups.note: Why each highlighted position, or variant from the literature, is shown, where its facts come from, and what stays open. Every row of the highlights file belongs to exactly one position group (check B25); the literature groups point to their case in the typed-variant test set. A sentence's source is a page (its URL), the release (by file) or a paper (paper:<slug>, listed under literature). ClinVar's classifications are quoted as ClinVar's, for the conditions it names; none is ChannelScope's.

why.text: c.1840C>T (p.Arg614Cys) is a known variant: ClinVar records it as VCV000012964, and this figure shows it as an example.
It changes the first base of codon 614, so that CGC (arginine) becomes TGC (cysteine).

ClinVar's expert panel classifies it as "Pathogenic; drug response", for "Malignant hyperthermia, susceptibility to, 1" and for toxicity responses to desflurane, enflurane, halothane, isoflurane, methoxyflurane, sevoflurane and succinylcholine.

why.text: Codon 142 is an example of a codon split by an intron: its first base, c.424, is the last base of exon 5, and its other two, c.425 and c.426, begin exon 6.

Spliced together, its bases read GGA, which codes glycine 142.
Codons 141 and 143, and the first and last bases of intron 5, are shown with it so that the split can be followed.

why.text: An in-frame deletion from the literature: three bases, c.7042 to c.7044 (GAG), are lost, so the reading frame is kept and one amino acid, glutamic acid 2348, is lost.

amino_acids_source.checked: Every code the standard genetic code produces, and every codon listed for it, against table 1 (check B19)

hgvs_names.note: ChannelScope's HGVS c. names at a test set of positions, so that a figure computing names for any position can be checked against ChannelScope's as well as its own. Exonic names are the codon map's; intronic names follow HGVS's rules, quoted below (check B20). A figure may compute names for any position on three conditions: the rule is HGVS's own, cited; this test set; and the article's check at every position.
hgvs_names.included: Every exon's first and last bases; every intron's first and last bases and its middle base, or both middle bases where it has an even number; both ends of each untranslated region; and the stop codon's three bases, which have no residue.

rules.says: numbering starts with c.1 at the A of the ATG translation initiation (start) codon and ends with the last nucleotide of the translation termination (stop) codon
nucleotides upstream (5') of the ATG-translation initiation codon (start) are marked with a - (hyphen-minus) and numbered c.-1, c.-2, c.-3, etc., going further upstream.
nucleotides downstream (3') of the translation termination codon (stop) are marked with a * (asterisk) and numbered c.*1, c.*2, c.*3, etc., going further downstream.
there is no nucleotide c.0.
nucleotides at the 5' end of an intron are numbered relative to the last nucleotide of the directly upstream exon, followed by a + (plus) and their position in the intron
nucleotides at the 3' end of an intron are numbered relative to the first nucleotide of the directly downstream exon, followed by a - (hyphen-minus) and their position away from that exon
in introns with an uneven number of nucleotides, the central nucleotide is numbered relative to the upstream exon followed by a + (plus)
a coding DNA reference sequence does not contain intron or 5' and 3' gene flanking sequences, and can therefore not be used as a reference to describe variants in these regions

typed_variants.note: What a figure needs to compute the consequence of a change a reader types. The test set to check it against is withheld from this release, as its README says. Nothing here is a release fact about any typed change.
typed_variants.label: computed from the sequence; not a clinical interpretation
conditions: The rules are HGVS's for names and normalisation, and the Sequence Ontology's for classes, each cited from its source.
ChannelScope keeps a test set of its computed consequences, with ClinVar's expert-panel variants as outside truth; this release withholds it, as its README says.
The article's second implementation covers every coding substitution and a spread of insertions and deletions.

A typed change is labelled as computed from the sequence and not a clinical interpretation. No pathogenicity is inferred from its class, and nothing is said of splicing or of the transcript's fate; both are stated as not computed.
A mismatched reference base is refused, and an intronic change gets its c. name and 'effect not computed'.
A typed change never becomes a release fact.
typed_variants.conditions_basis: The six conditions of 2026-09-29, with two forms from HGVS added for v0.4: a name with an intronic position is written NC_000019.10(NM_000540.3):c.…, and a computed protein name in parentheses; and the splice-site flag, decided by the operator on 2026-10-03.

rules.says: the 3'rule applies to ALL descriptions (genome, gene, transcript, and protein) of a given variant.

the 3' rule is not applied when there is a deletion/duplication around exon/exon junctions with identical nucleotides flanking the junction, where shifting the variant 3' would place it in the next exon.
rules.applied: ChannelScope shifts on the genome, where an intron separates every two exons, so the exception holds without a special case.

rules.says: when a description is possible according to several types, the preferred description is: (1) substitution, (2) deletion, (3) inversion, (4) duplication, (5) insertion.
when a variant can be described as a duplication or an insertion, prioritisation determines it should be described as a duplication.
changes involving two or more consecutive nucleotides are described as deletion/insertion (delins) variants.
Inversion: a sequence change where, compared to a reference sequence, more than one nucleotide replacing the original sequence is the reverse complement of the original sequence.
descriptions should make clear whether the change was experimentally determined or theoretically deduced by giving predicted consequences in parentheses.

classes.definition: A transcript variant occurring within an intron.
A UTR variant of the 5' UTR.
A UTR variant of the 3' UTR.
A codon variant that changes at least one base of the canonical start codon.
A sequence variant where at least one base in the terminator codon is changed, but the terminator remains.
A sequence variant where there is no resulting change to the encoded amino acid.
A sequence variant whereby at least one base of a codon is changed, resulting in a premature stop codon, leading to a shortened polypeptide.
A sequence variant where at least one base of the terminator codon (stop) is changed, resulting in an elongated transcript.
A sequence variant whereby at least one of the bases in the terminator codon is changed.
A sequence variant which causes a disruption of the translational reading frame, because the number of nucleotides inserted or deleted is not a multiple of three.
An inframe non synonymous variant that inserts bases into in the coding sequence.
An inframe non synonymous variant that deletes bases from the coding sequence.
A sequence variant, that changes one or more bases, resulting in a different amino acid sequence but where the length is preserved.

typed_variants.class_order: A change is classed by the first of these that applies: wholly in an intron, intron_variant; across an exon-intron boundary, left unclassed, with its effect not computed; wholly in an untranslated region, 5_prime_UTR_variant or 3_prime_UTR_variant; touching the start codon, start_lost; leaving the protein unchanged, stop_retained_variant if it touches the stop codon, else synonymous_variant; making the first changed residue a stop, or, in a change that keeps the reading frame, one of the residues it puts in, stop_gained; touching the stop codon and lengthening the protein, stop_lost; touching the stop codon where reading meets no stop before the transcript's end and no more residues are read than the reference has, terminator_codon_variant, since the protein's length cannot be told; changing the coding length by other than a multiple of three, frameshift_variant; otherwise inframe_insertion, inframe_deletion or missense_variant. The order is ChannelScope's; each class is SO's, with SO's definition.
class_order_reading: A change's place is the bases it replaces or deletes. An insertion's is the two bases either side of it, and a duplication's is where its copy goes, between the last base it duplicates and the next, even when the copy holds intronic bases: what splicing makes of such a copy is not computed, and the splice-site flag shows the zones it touches.

A protein whose reading meets no stop before the transcript's end is longer than the reference when more residues are read than the reference has (case d28); otherwise its length cannot be told (cases d29 and d30).

A stop the change puts in is a new stop, so the class is stop_gained; a deletion that brings the reference's own stop codon forward, so that the first changed residue is a stop, is stop_gained too, named as a nonsense change (case d38).

refusals.note: Changes the engine refuses, each with the reason it gives; rows of the test set's 'refused' set. A refused change gets no name and no class.
kinds: A range written on NM_000540.3 alone whose two ends are exonic and lie in different exons. On the coding reference they are read as the transcript joins them, with no intron between (HGVS, Numbering, line 40); on the genome an intron lies between them. The same range is taken on the genomic reference, NC_000019.10(NM_000540.3) (refused: cases d51 and d56; taken: case d52).
An insertion written on NM_000540.3 alone between two such neighbours: on the genome it has no single place (case r02).
A change that HGVS's 3' rule carries to c.*144, the last base of the genome this release holds: past it the rule cannot be followed, so the name cannot be settled (case r01).

splice_flag.note: Decided by the operator on 2026-10-03, with both triggers. The flag names where a change sits, by the Sequence Ontology's definitions, and predicts nothing. It does not change the class or the protein shown.
triggers: The change lies in a splice site or in SO's splice region.
A deletion or duplication has an equally valid placement that does, even when its HGVS name does not.

terms.definition: Intronic 2 bp region bordering the exon, at the 5' edge of the intron. A splice_site that is downstream_adjacent_to exon and starts intron.
Intronic 2 bp region bordering the exon, at the 3' edge of the intron. A splice_site that is upstream_adjacent_to exon and finishes intron.
A region surrounding a cis_splice site, either within 1-3 bases of the exon or 3-8 bases of the intron.

reading: A substitution, deletion, deletion-insertion or inversion lies in a zone if any base it replaces or deletes does.
A duplication lies in a zone if any base it duplicates does, or if its copy goes between two bases that both lie in zones.
An insertion lies in a zone only if the two bases either side of it both do.
Exon 1's start and exon 106's end have no intron beside them, so no zone.

A duplication's equally valid placements are every place its copy can go without changing the sequence, each written as HGVS would write a change there: a duplication where the copy follows the bases it repeats, otherwise an insertion. Each lies in a zone by the reading for its own form (case b15; made explicit in v0.5).
splice_flag.shows: SO's term with its ID; for the second trigger, each equal placement and the terms it touches; and that splicing is not computed.
splice_flag.never_shows: That splicing is disrupted, how likely that is, or any score.
splice_flag.correction: The brief's amendment of 2026-10-03 named splice_region_variant (SO:0001630) for the splice region. In SO's release 2026-08-07 that term is a kind of splicing_variant, "A sequence variant that changes the process of splicing.", so naming it would imply the effect the flag must never claim. The flag names the region term, splice_region (SO:0001902), whose definition gives the same bounds (check B24).

columns.region, so_term, so_id: where the change lies, and its SO class
columns.p_hgvs: the predicted protein name; empty where the effect is not computed
columns.first_changed_residue, protein_end, new_: numbered on P21817-1: the first residue at which the new protein differs from P21817-1 (for a duplication, the residue after the copy), the new protein's last residue, and the codon of its stop

caption.one_idea: Nine-tenths of the stretch of chromosome 19 that this RYR1 transcript spans is intron; spliced together, its exons hold the coding sequence between two untranslated ends, and that sequence is read three bases at a time into the protein's 5,038 amino acids.
caption.caption_body: RYR1 on GRCh38, transcript NM_000540.3 (Ensembl ENST00000359596.8, MANE Select), chromosome 19, plus strand. Exon bounds and coding bounds are from ChannelScope's evidence graph; residue numbering follows UniProt P21817-1, which is identical to RefSeq NP_000531.2. Coding parts of exons are solid, untranslated parts outlined, and introns are omitted from the second panel. Positions with no residue — introns and untranslated regions — are drawn as such and never assigned to a neighbouring residue.
gaps: untranslated regions of exons 1 and 106: no residue
a codon split across an intron is drawn across the gap, not within one exon

scope_and_limits: This release carries the genome leg only: GRCh38 to transcript to codon to residue. It does NOT carry the human-to-rabbit residue mapping, which ChannelScope's release ryr1_mappings_v0.1 carries.

It changes from exon_map_v0.5.2 only texts, and what it carries, so that it can be published. Six texts that named the article by working names now name the article. The results of comparing the typed-variant engine's names with an independent implementation's are withheld, since that implementation's terms of use have not been read, and so is the typed-variant test set, which holds its names; the header still cites the test set by case. NHGRI's terms are quoted, now that they have been read. Statements that were no longer true are corrected: the human-to-rabbit mapping is in a release, and the code's licence is chosen. Its engine, test cases and data are v0.5.1's, byte for byte, and so v0.5's but for case s01's description, which v0.5.1 changed: the exon table, highlights, c. names and three sequence files are v0.5.1's files under this release's names, so the exonic and protein files' title lines still name exon_map_v0.5, whose build wrote them. manifest.json lists every change.
A typed change is computed from the sequence and is not a clinical interpretation. Splicing, the transcript's fate, and any effect on the protein's structure or function are not computed.
ClinVar's classifications are quoted as ClinVar's, for the conditions it names. None is ChannelScope's.
This release carries CC BY 4.0 for the parts ChannelScope holds rights in (licence); the sources' terms are quoted under terms.
The papers quoted were read from snapshots that are not redistributed. Two, Sato 2008 and Zhou 2007, were read from PDFs the operator supplied, because their publishers refused the tool's requests.
This release holds no data for a figure of the human-to-rabbit mapping; that mapping is in ChannelScope's release ryr1_mappings_v0.1.

This view release serves the article's exon-map figure only. ChannelScope's other releases, published beside it, carry the residue mappings (ryr1_mappings_v0.1), the structures' measured states (ryr1_structure_states_v0.1) and the evidence composed for a residue set (ryr1_composition_v0.1).
